architecture.mechanism: **Standardized, vendor-neutral methodology for real-time resource consumption verification and independent auditing protocols**
architecture.intervention: Deploy a **real-time condenser tube fouling monitoring system** using **independent, third-party auditing protocols** to continuously measure and verify condenser tube cleanliness via **transport boundary-defined metering** (e.g., ultrasonic or optical sensors calibrated to a "Two-Meter Water Method" equivalent for scale detection). Integrate with existing water treatment systems to trigger **predictive maintenance alerts** when fouling exceeds a predefined threshold, enabling targeted cleaning within the 48-hour shutdown window.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduce condensing temperature spikes and capacity loss by **proactively identifying fouling** before it impacts performance, while maintaining compliance with water treatment constraints. Expected outcome: **≤3% capacity degradation at peak load** and **≤15% kW/ton increase**, achieved through data-driven intervention timing.
architecture.falsification_test: Install sensors and validate that fouling detection triggers maintenance **within 24 hours of a 0.5°C condensing temperature rise**, confirmed via independent audit logs (cross-referenced with PUCT-compliant metering standards). Compare pre- and post-intervention capacity/kW/ton metrics under identical load conditions.
